count_jobs.description: Count the jobs that match any mix of filters, without listing them: keywords, remote or on-site, visa sponsorship, tags, job type, company, location, country and how recently they were posted. The count comes split by country, by the day each job was posted, by company and by tag, with how many are remote and how many state their pay. Use it for a weekly market report or to watch demand for a skill: 'how many Python jobs went up in Switzerland this week'. It reads every page it is allowed to rather than stopping at a number of results, and says how much of the board that was.

count_jobs.name: count_jobs

parameters.description: Words the job has to contain. Every word must appear, but it can appear anywhere in the posting: the title, the company, the location, the tags or the description. Leave empty to skip keyword matching.
parameters.name: keywords

parameters.description: Only return jobs the board marks as remote, or only ones it does not. Leave empty for both.
parameters.name: remote

parameters.description: Narrow to jobs that offer visa sponsorship, or to ones that do not. This is the one filter Arbeitnow applies itself, through its 'visa_sponsorship' query parameter, so which postings qualify is its call and not this integration's. Leave empty for both.
parameters.name: visa_sponsorship

parameters.description: Only return jobs carrying one of these tags, matched case-insensitively anywhere in the tag. The board's tags are free text and the vocabulary changes with what is posted, so run 'List tags' first to see which ones are in use rather than guessing: a tag nobody is using returns nothing. Leave empty for every tag.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Only return jobs of one of these employment types or seniorities, matched case-insensitively anywhere in the value. The board files both under one field, so an employment type such as 'full time' and a seniority such as 'mid-senior' are both looked for here. The vocabulary is free text, so run 'List job types' to see which values are in use. Leave empty for every type.
parameters.name: job_types

parameters.description: Only return jobs whose company name contains this text, matched case-insensitively. Leave empty for every company.
parameters.name: company

parameters.description: Only return jobs whose location contains this text, matched case-insensitively. Leave empty for everywhere.
parameters.name: location

parameters.description: Only return jobs in this country. The board lists jobs in Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Switzerland and the Netherlands, each on its own site, and a job's country is the site it is listed on, so this finds a London job that only says 'Remote' in its location. Write the country's name, or a short form such as UK or DE. Leave empty for every country.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: Only return jobs posted this many days ago or less. Leave empty for everything the scan reads.
parameters.name: posted_within_days

parameters.description: How much of the board to count, from 1 to 10 pages of up to 300 jobs each. The counts describe the jobs this reads, not the whole board, and 'scanned_count' says how many that was. Pages already read by an earlier step in the same run are reused, so the counting actions together cost one pass, not one each. Defaults to 3.
parameters.name: max_pages

parameters.description: How many of the busiest companies and the commonest tags to list, from 1 to 100 each. Every country and every day is listed whatever this is, and 'company_count' still counts every company. Defaults to 10.
parameters.name: max_results

parameters.description: How much of each row to print into the run output for a person to read. Every row that was returned is listed either way, however many that is: the result limit above decides that, not this field. 'One line each' gives the job, the company, the place, how long ago it was posted and the slug that 'Get a job' takes; 'Every field' adds the tags, the exact posting date, the link and the description. This only changes what is displayed, never what is saved: a later step sees the same data whichever is chosen. Defaults to one line each.

get_job.description: Fetch one job by its slug, with the full description both as plain text and as the original HTML. The API has no per-job route, so this reads the board a page at a time until the slug turns up, up to ten pages. Take the slug from a listing step rather than typing one: the board publishes only what is open right now, so a role that has been filled or has expired is gone from it and is reported as not found.

description: Search the Arbeitnow job board through its keyless public API. Arbeitnow is a Berlin job board for roles with visa sponsorship, remote work and four-day weeks, listing jobs in Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Switzerland and the Netherlands: list the newest openings, search them by keyword, company, tag, employment type, city or country, pull the jobs posted since a scheduled run last checked, count what is on offer by country and day, find the postings that state their pay, and see who is hiring. No account or API key is required.
